# Web Search

The Apify actor [`apify/web-search`](https://apify.com/apify/web-search) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.20**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Search the web and get organic results as JSON with title, URL, snippet, and position. You can filter by date, country, language, and domain. The Actor provides a real-time API.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Google Search Result $0.005, Actor Start $0.00005, DuckDuckGo Search Result $0.005 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/web-search) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-web-search@0.0.20#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      query: "…"
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes |  | Search query — Operators like site: pass through unchecked. Use allowedDomains and blockedDomains to enforce domain filters, and dateFrom and dateTo for dates. |
| `provider` | string |  | `"google"` | Provider — Google is the default search engine, supports location, and returns the most data. DuckDuckGo has no location, covers fewer countries, and fills fewer fields. Use it for a second, independent ranking, or when Google finds nothing. Each search is charged separately. |
| `maxResults` | integer |  |  | Maximum results — Maximum number of organic results to return. Leave it empty to get every result on the page. You get fewer when the page has fewer, or when domain filters remove some. |
| `languageCode` | string |  | `"en"` | Language code — ISO 639-1 code with an optional region suffix, like "en", "de", or "pt-BR". See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes. Google uses it to localize the interface and bias ranking, without translating or strictly filtering results. DuckDuckGo picks the matching re |
| `countryCode` | string |  | `"US"` | Country code — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, like "US", "DE", or "CZ". The search runs as if you were in that country, changing result order and which local businesses appear. Google queries that country's domain (google.de for "DE"). DuckDuckGo picks the matching region, preferring the languageCode vari |
| `location` | string |  |  | Location — A place name, most specific first, like "Paris, Ile-de-France, France". Google treats it as your location for local and "near me" results. It doesn't filter pages. It's best-effort and not validated: Google may ignore places it can't resolve. Using it with DuckDuckGo returns INVALID_PARAM |
| `dateFrom` | string |  |  | Date from — The earliest publication date to include. Best-effort. See the README. |
| `dateTo` | string |  |  | Date to — The latest publication date to include. Best-effort. See the README. |
| `allowedDomains` | string[] |  |  | Allowed domains — Return only results from these domains. You can list up to 10 domains. A domain matches itself and its subdomains, so "wikipedia.org" covers "en.wikipedia.org". A top-level domain like "gov" matches every domain under it. Examples: "wikipedia.org", "docs.python.org", "gov". |
| `blockedDomains` | string[] |  |  | Blocked domains — Exclude results from these domains. You can list up to 10 domains. Matching works like allowedDomains, including subdomains and top-level domains. Examples: "pinterest.com", "reddit.com", "ru". |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
